note: M37 P4: read_corpus lifts each entry's shot and the shot side of its refusals (the M37 plan's decision 5 and call 3). CorpusSwing gains shot, the survivor's artifact's ShotData whole (analysis.json's swing.shot for a swing, shot_analysis.json's shot for a photo entry, never a duplicate's), and shot_unscored, that artifact's unscored entries less every CHECKPOINT_REGISTRY name. A swing's shot the contract refuses stays shot_needs_review and is not carried. Both keys are written only when set (M37 P3), so a corpus with neither serializes as it did at 2. What the dry run found, and what this declares: the key shot is added on every recorded corpus entry whose artifact holds a readable shot, at expected.corpus.swings[i].shot and, in storage/corpus/real, at the same entries under expected.narrowed.club-3w and club-7i; and the same key on each career case that adopts one of those corpora, at input.corpus.swings[i].shot. The storage cases are conflicting-shot-photos, every-source, mishit-ineligible, one-photo-two-clips, real and shot-review, recorded from frozen Python, and five hand-worked M35 cases whose photo entries carry a shot_analysis.json (mixed-session, no-face-on-and-no-photo, photo-entries-one-photo, photo-entry-pooled, photo-entry-repairs). A duplicate's shot is in none of them, and shot-review's shot that lacks a required key is not carried. No recorded artifact's unscored holds a flight row or a photo-side key (the real corpus's analyses were recorded with measurements and shot alone), so no vector gains shot_unscored; the reader's own tests hold that lift. Nothing moves: no pooled swing, no count, no aggregate and no report reads either field. career_version moves 2 -> 3 on every storage and career vector. Every value not listed here stays the one it was.
